criteria.commensurate: Yes. The bookend is +3.4 pct total (17.7 to 18.3 s, +0.6 s). Homesteads at 15 hh are +0.80 s summed (4.51 to 5.31 s), which is the pass less what the tie-break saves. 40 hh is -11.5 pct, 20 hh -0.4 pct, 10 hh +0.8 pct. Seed 4 +17.6 pct (crosses the 10 pct seed line, not 20 pct) is web/hinterland/notice, the layout effect of the 20 ft gap. The control shows this effect going both ways (15/4 and 15/39 notice rise with main gap). It is not added work, and homesteads on seed 4 is only +0.05 s.
criteria.necessary: Yes. The 20 ft homestead gap (grow_gap, FR-011) and the gap pass (gap_ways.lay_the_ways, FR-014) are option A, which the GM chose in Amendment 3 for the shape of the map. The control perf-318-control-gap-pass puts the rise on them: with the pass stubbed, homesteads at 15 hh fall below main (3.14 s against 4.42 s), and with main's gap seed 4 web and hinterland return to main.
criteria.no_way_around: None left that I would hold the verdict on. The round-4 remedy (flood, way_out and trace reading lists, byte-identical: diff reviewed, test_gap_ways 12 pass) is in at cdd1bc379. It took 0.66 s off the 15 hh homesteads between end records 014912Z and 015841Z, as I measured for the flood. The pass is now about 0.4-0.6 s a map. What remains is the corridor loop in lane_layers, 0.075-0.107 s a map (25-35k hit_points calls). It could be vectorized as a mask beside hit_points, about 0.1 s a map or 2 pct of the total. That is recommended, not owed. Seed 4 has nothing left to cut, because its growth is in web, hinterland and notice.
